title: The Peacock's Dance on the Terrace (KN)
summary: A vain prince boasts of his flawless elegance. Birbal uses the peacock's dance to remind him that even the most beautiful creatures have humble feet. [KN]
full_text:
A visiting young prince from Rajputana was celebrated for his dazzling physical beauty, tall stature, and fashionable silk attire. However, he was insufferably conceited, spending hours admiring himself in mirrors and openly mocking the plain features of older scholars in Akbar's court.

During an afternoon reception on the palace terrace overlooking the gardens, a wild peacock flew onto the marble balustrade. The bird spread its magnificent tail into a giant fan of shimmering emerald, sapphire, and bronze feathers, dancing gracefully in the breeze.

The young prince exclaimed: 'Look at that peacock! It possesses supreme beauty, like myself! It has no flaw in all creation!'

Birbal smiled gently: 'Prince, observe the peacock closely as it dances.'

As the magnificent bird completed its graceful turn, its eyes glanced down at its own legs. Its feet were coarse, wrinkled, grey, and scaly, covered in dirt and sharp claws.

The instant the peacock looked down at its ugly feet, it ceased its proud dance, dropped its tail, and let out a harsh, mournful shriek: *Kaa-ooo! Kaa-ooo!*

Birbal said to the young prince:

'You see, noble Prince? The peacock has the most magnificent feathers in the world, yet the moment it glances down at its coarse, wrinkled feet, its vanity is shattered, and it weeps with shame!

'Nature has given every human being some gift of beauty, intelligence, or strength, but nature has also given every mortal coarse "feet of clay"—flaws, vulnerabilities, and mortality—to remind us to remain humble!

'He who gazes only upon his glittering feathers becomes an arrogant fool. But he who remembers his humble feet walks through life with grace, kindness, and modesty.'

The young prince stood silent. The lesson touched his conscience deeply. He bowed to Birbal, apologized to the elders, and resolved to cultivate inner virtue above outward vanity.
